from /ui/theme import ThemeScope
use /ui
from /ui/components/project-indicator import ProjectIndicator
from ./project-tab import RibbonProjectTabScope
from ./code-tab import RibbonCodeTabScope
from ./spec-tab import RibbonSpecTabScope

from /scope/user-preferences import UserPreferencesScope

export ui-component RibbonScope:
    concept: {RibbonConcept}

concept RibbonConcept:
    pitch:
        The ribbon along the top of the main window: tabs, each holding the
        application's commands for one area of work in labelled groups.

    shape: {RibbonShape}

shape RibbonShape:
    description:
        A ribbon runs along the top of the window, using gpui-kit's Tab
        component with its default styling, borders, and spacing, only in the
        @{ThemeScope}'s colours. Nothing adds to or takes away from a tab's own
        borders or margins, so a tab's label never shifts as tabs open and
        close. Along the top of the commands, a line in the colour of the tabs'
        own side borders runs from the far left, beneath the project indicator,
        to the side border of the first open tab, and on from that tab's other
        side border to the next open tab or the far right. An open tab meets
        the commands beneath it with no line between them, its side borders
        running straight down to where the line picks up again. There is no
        other line there, not even a faint one at a fractional display scale.

        A tab whose commands work on one of the chat input's modes, as the Code
        and Spec tabs do, takes that mode's colour: its label is in the mode's
        colour while the tab is closed, and while open, the tab is tinted with
        it instead and its label is the tab's own colour. Each such tab says
        more. Its tabs are, in order: Project,
        Code, Spec, Research, and Application. The window always opens on
        Project. Beneath the tabs, the selected tab's commands sit in groups.
        There is no raw output view and no toggle for one.

    keyboard:
        <Alt+1> opens the first tab, <Alt+2> the second, and so on, through
        each tab in the order the tabs are shown, <Alt+5> opening Application.
        Each opens its tab alone, as clicking it does, and expands the ribbon
        first if it is collapsed. A number past the last tab does nothing. Like
        the ribbon's other shortcuts, they do nothing while an inset panel is
        open. A tab's tooltip doesn't give its shortcut, since a tab has no
        tooltip.

    openingSeveralTabs:
        Clicking a tab opens it alone, as usual. Ctrl+clicking one (Cmd+click on
        macOS) opens it alongside whichever tabs are already open, or, if it is
        already open, closes it, so any number of tabs can be open at once. The
        last open tab can't be closed this way: Ctrl+clicking it leaves it open.
        Every open tab shows as selected.

        The command area then holds the groups of every open tab side by side,
        in the order of the tabs rather than the order they were opened, with no
        divider between one tab's groups and the next, as between any groups. An
        open tab with no commands adds nothing, and "No commands yet" shows only
        when none of the open tabs has any. When the groups are wider than the
        window, the command area scrolls sideways. The command area stays the
        same height however many tabs are open.

        Double-clicking a tab still collapses the ribbon, and expanding it again
        shows the same tabs open. Which tabs are open isn't kept between
        launches: the window always opens with only Project open.

    activity:
        The indicator and list of the @{RunningActivityScope} sit just to the
        right of the project indicator, as it is beside the tabs or leading the
        collapsed ribbon.

    projectIndicator:
        At the left end of the bar sits the @{ProjectIndicator}, a solid block
        the full height of the bar, left of the tab bar itself rather than
        inside it, so the tab bar's own padding and bottom line don't reach it.
        There is no divider between it and what follows: the change of
        background is the edge. The activity spinner leads the tab bar, just
        after it.

    groups:
        Each group has its title in muted text rotated -90deg (bottom to top)
        aligned along the left edge of the group naming what its commands have
        in common. The title sits on a strip with a slightly different
        background colour, at 12px, with generous padding either side of it
        within the strip, which runs the full height of the commands' area, with
        no padding above or below it, 8 pixels from the buttons beside it. The
        first group's strip sits flush against the left edge of the commands'
        area, with no space before it. Groups sit side by side, 8 pixels apart, with no
        divider between them: each group's title strip is what marks where it
        starts.

        A tab with no commands reads "No commands yet".

    tabs:
        Each tab is a scope of its own, which says what groups and commands it
        holds, and what each command does.

        project: @{RibbonProjectTabScope}

        code: @{RibbonCodeTabScope}

        spec: @{RibbonSpecTabScope}

        research: @{RibbonResearchTabScope}

        application: @{RibbonApplicationTabScope}

    commands:
        A command button is one of two sizes, and each tab says which of its
        commands are which:
        - full: as tall as the buttons' room inside their padding, its large icon above its label
        - slim: 22 pixels tall, its small icon to the left of its label

        Buttons side by side are 8 pixels apart. Slim buttons side by side
        stack down instead, top aligned, three to a column, each column as wide
        as its widest button and each button as wide as its column; a fourth
        starts the next column, 8 pixels along. A full button always stands
        alone.

        Every button is square, with no rounded corners. Its background is
        clearly apart from the commands' area behind it, though still quiet:
        white laid a seventh of the way over that area in dark mode, and not
        quite half way in light mode, rather than a colour of its own, so it
        stays as far apart from a tinted body too, lighter in both modes, and more so while hovered; while
        pressed it darkens instead. An on or off setting, like dark mode, is a
        switch rather than a button, sitting in a block the size and colour of
        a button of its size.

        A command's tooltip explains what it does rather than repeating its
        label, and gives its keyboard shortcut if it has one.

        A command can be marked primary; each tab says which of its commands
        are.

        A command that can't run is disabled, not hidden, and its tooltip says
        why.

    height:
        The command area is the same height on every tab, even one with no
        commands, so the window beneath doesn't move when switching tabs: 98
        pixels, with 8 pixels of padding at the right end but none at the left:
        the first group's title strip starts right at the command area's left
        edge. "No commands yet" keeps 8 pixels from that edge. The buttons are padded 8
        pixels above and below, leaving them 82 pixels, room for a full button
        or three slim buttons with 8 pixels between each; the groups' title
        strips are not padded, and run the full 98 pixels.

    collapsing:
        The ribbon collapses, and expands again, with a chevron button at the
        right end of the ribbon, by double-clicking a tab, or with Ctrl+F1
        (Cmd+F1 on macOS). Whether it is collapsed is one of the
        @{UserPreferencesScope}.

        Collapsed, the tabs go away too. The ribbon becomes a single thin row
        led by the project indicator, the same solid block as beside the tabs,
        filling the row's height, with no divider after it, then the activity
        spinner, and then every primary command, from all of
        the tabs, as small buttons: a small icon beside its label, and dark mode
        as a small switch. They keep the order of their tabs, with a thin
        vertical divider between the commands of one tab and the next, and keep
        their tooltips and disabled states. The chevron sits at the right end of
        the row. Every control in the row, the chevron and the dividers
        included, is vertically centred in it.

# Piton fluency

Piton is a declarative, whitespace-structured language for describing agentic
skills, agents, commands, and reference documents. It has no runtime: it
compiles to data (JSON, YAML) or, through a framework, to Markdown. Source
files use the `.pi` extension.

## Syntax

```piton
// A comment. Comments are line-only.
myVariable: 42                       // a number
myString: Strings are unquoted       // a string
myQuoted: "false"                    // quoting forces a string
myTyped:: string:: number: 42        // constraints, first match wins

myList:
    - one
    - two
myInlineList: [one, two, three]

myDictionary:
    nested:
        deep: value

computed: {1 + 2}                    // `{ }` evaluates; bare text does not
interpolated: Hello, ${myString}

anchor Base:
    name: Base
    summary: This is ${this.name}  // `this` pins to Base

anchor Child extends Base:
    name: Child
    detail: This is ${self.name}   // `self` follows the child
    summary: ${super.summary} and more

abstract anchor Shape as shape:      // `as` registers a keyword
    description:: string

shape Concrete:                      // same as `extends Shape`
    description: Implemented

from ./other import Thing, Other Alias
from ./other export *
use ./keywords
export anchor Published:
    value: 1
```

## Reserved words

`anchor`, `abstract`, `extends`, `as`, `export`, `from`, `import`, `use`, `this`, `self`, `super`, `true`, `false`, `null`

## Types

`string`, `number`, `boolean`, `null`, `list`, `dictionary`, `anchor`, `any`, `simple`, `complex`

Literals: `true`, `false`, `null`

content.text:
The New Project button no longer grows when the ribbon is minimized, and when the minimized row is too narrow its buttons now scroll sideways. The full test suite passes (219 passed, 1 ignored), both builds have no warnings, and the piton checks and build pass.

**Cause:** slim buttons were set to fill their parent's full width. That's correct in the full ribbon, where they stack in columns, but the minimized row reused the same button, so each button tried to fill the whole row. New Project comes first, so it took over: 1736px wide in a 1920px window. The Dark mode block had the same problem.

**Spec** (`spec/ui/components/ribbon/index.pi`):
- There's a new **small** button size, used only in the minimized ribbon: as tall as a slim button, but only as wide as its icon and label.
- It now states that no button ever stretches to fill a row, and that a slim command stays small when the ribbon is minimized.
- When the commands don't fit, the stretch between the project indicator and the chevron scrolls sideways. The indicator and chevron stay in place and nothing shrinks to fit.

**Code:**
- `src/ribbon/mod.rs` adds the small size, which the minimized row now uses; slim buttons still fill their column.
- The row is now three parts: the indicator, the scrolling middle with the spinner, commands and dividers, and the chevron. The two ends never shrink.
- `src/ribbon/application_tab.rs` gives the Dark mode block a small version that is only as wide as its switch.

**Test:** `ribbon_tabs_hold_their_controls` in `src/main_window.rs` now checks the minimized row:
- each command is under 160px wide, in order and not touching the next;
- at a 360px window width, the indicator and chevron stay inside the window while the commands run past the edge instead of shrinking;
- scrolling sideways brings Settings, the last command, into view.

With the old sizing put back, the test fails on exactly this bug.

This change applies to the minimized row only. The full ribbon's command area already scrolled sideways, and I didn't change the tab bar, which cuts off rather than scrolls if the window is narrower than the tabs. I also haven't looked at it in the running app.
